dialogue.content: ■よろしくお願いします。
dialogue.English: Thank you for meeting with me.

dialogue.content: こんにちは。本日はよろしくお願いいたします
dialogue.English: Hello. It's a pleasure to speak with you today.

dialogue.content: お時間早いですが、準備がよろしければ始めたいのですが、大丈夫でしょうか？
dialogue.English: We're a little early, but if you're ready, I'd like to begin. Is that alright with you?

dialogue.content: ■大丈夫です。
dialogue.English: Yes, that's fine.

dialogue.content: ありがとございます。では、始めますね
dialogue.English: Thank you. Let's begin, then.

dialogue.content: こんにちは。相談員です。本日はどのような相談でしょうか？
dialogue.English: Hello, I'm your counselor. What would you like to discuss today?

dialogue.content: 小5の息子が言うこと聞かなくてイライラが限界です。
dialogue.English: My fifth-grade son won't listen to me, and I'm at the end of my rope.

dialogue.content: お子さんのことでお困りなんですね。どんなことでイライラしてしまうのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: It sounds like you're having a difficult time with your son. What kinds of things make you feel frustrated?

dialogue.content: 朝はギリギリまで寝て登校班に遅れてもあわてて走るでもなく、遅れても謝るでもなく。忘れ物も多いし、ゲームばかりやってるし、出したものも何度言っても片付けないし、宿題もやらないし。
dialogue.English: In the morning, he sleeps until the last minute. Even if he's late for his school walking group, he doesn't rush or apologize. He's always forgetting things, plays video games all the time, won't clean up after himself no matter how many times I tell him, and he doesn't do his homework.

dialogue.content: 塾もサボり始めた様で、ぶっ叩いてやりたいです。
dialogue.English: It seems he's started skipping his cram school too. I just want to smack him.

dialogue.content: いろいろと頭を抱えることばかりで大変なですね。叩いてしまいたくなるくらい、いらっとしますよね
dialogue.English: It must be very difficult with so many things to worry about. It's understandable to feel so irritated you want to hit him.

dialogue.content: 息子さんは、毎日このようなかんじですか？
dialogue.English: Is your son like this every day?

dialogue.content: もう毎日で何度言っても聞かなくて、こっちも疲れてきました。
dialogue.English: Yes, every single day. He won't listen no matter how many times I tell him, and I'm getting exhausted.

dialogue.content: 毎日だとしんどいですよねどんな感じでお子さんに注意されるのでしょう？
dialogue.English: It must be draining every day. How do you usually reprimand your child?

dialogue.content: 最初は普通に言うんですけど、あーとか生返事で行動に移さないので段々言い方がきつくなってきます。
dialogue.English: At first, I speak to him normally, but he just gives me a noncommittal "uh-huh" and doesn't do anything, so my tone gradually gets harsher.

dialogue.content: すぐにやらないとこちらもいらっとしますよね。言い方が変わると息子さんはやりますか？
dialogue.English: It's frustrating when they don't do it right away, isn't it? When your tone changes, does your son do what you ask?

dialogue.content: 全然なのでムカつきます。ご飯なんかダラダラと2時間以上かけてます。
dialogue.English: Not at all, which is infuriating. He'll dawdle over his meals for more than two hours.

dialogue.content: 本人が
dialogue.English: He himself...

dialogue.content: ええ
dialogue.English: Mmm-hmm.

dialogue.content: 中学受験したいと言うので塾にも行かせてるのに。夫はもう時間と金の無駄だって。
dialogue.English: ...said he wanted to take the entrance exams for middle school, which is why I'm sending him to cram school. But my husband says it's a waste of time and money.

dialogue.content: 息子さんの意志を尊重されて行かせている塾のことも、夫さんはやめたほうがいいと思っているのですね。確かに、さぼるようになってしまったら、ショックですよね
dialogue.English: So your husband thinks he should quit the cram school you sent him to out of respect for his wishes. It certainly must be a shock that he's started to skip it.

dialogue.content: 夫さんは、息子さんに対してはどうでしょうか？注意とかされますか？
dialogue.English: What about your husband? How does he interact with your son? Does he ever discipline him?

dialogue.content: 夫は呑気なもんです。
dialogue.English: My husband is pretty carefree about it.

dialogue.content: 息子さんには寛大な感じなんですね。
dialogue.English: It sounds like he's quite lenient with your son.

dialogue.content: お話の途中ですが本日は何とお呼びすればよろしいでしょうか？
dialogue.English: I'm sorry to interrupt, but what should I call you today?

dialogue.content: 貴子でお願いします。
dialogue.English: Please call me Takako.

dialogue.content: 夫は半ば諦めてるんですかね。呆れてるというか。
dialogue.English: Maybe my husband has half given up on him—or rather, he's exasperated.

dialogue.content: 受験しないならしないでそういってくれれば済むんですけど、こんなんでも受験するって頑固で。
dialogue.English: If he's not going to take the exams, it would be easier if he just said so. But even while acting like this, he's stubborn about taking them.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。なるほど。息子さんは受験の意志はまだあるのですね。それだと、もっと真剣に取り組んでほしいですよね
dialogue.English: Thank you. I see. So your son still intends to take the exams. In that case, you must wish he would take it more seriously.

dialogue.content: 貴子さんは、今は息子さんには勉強してもらいたいかんじですか？
dialogue.English: Takako, do you feel that you want your son to focus on his studies right now?

dialogue.content: 本当に、やるんだかやらないんだか。本人が受験したいなら勉強はしてほしいです。最初の頃は少し余裕もあったんですが段々成績が落ちてきて。このままでは受かりません。
dialogue.English: Honestly, I don't know if he's going to do it or not. If he wants to take the exams, I want him to study. At first, he was doing okay, but his grades have been gradually dropping. At this rate, he won't pass.

dialogue.content: なるほど。成績に出てきてしまっているのですね。それだと、心配になりますよね。息子さん本人は成績のことは知っているのですか？
dialogue.English: I see. So it's starting to show in his grades. That must be worrisome. Does your son himself know about his grades?

dialogue.content: 知っていますね。受験対策の塾で、最初の頃は良かったんですけど。
dialogue.English: He knows. At the exam-prep cram school, things were good at first, but...

dialogue.content: ええ
dialogue.English: Mmm-hmm.

dialogue.content: 夫の言うようにお金の無駄なのかしら？
dialogue.English: I wonder if it's a waste of money, like my husband says.

dialogue.content: 夫さんはお金を無駄にしているとお感じで、貴子さんはお金のことより勉強というかんじでしょうか？
dialogue.English: So your husband feels it's a waste of money, while you are more concerned about his studies than the cost?

dialogue.content: 本人がやりたいと言い出したことだし、頑張るならお金は出してでも受験させたいです。
dialogue.English: Since he was the one who said he wanted to do it, if he's willing to work hard, I want to support him with the exam even if it costs money.

dialogue.content: そうですよね。本人の意思を尊重してあげたいお気持ちわかります。息子さんは、学校ではどのような感じでお過ごしですか？
dialogue.English: I understand. I can see you want to respect his wishes. What is your son like at school?

dialogue.content: でも、こんなんじゃ…頭にきます。
dialogue.English: But, with the way things are... it makes me angry.

dialogue.content: 確かにもっと勉強してほしいですよね
dialogue.English: Indeed, you'd like him to study more.

dialogue.content: 学校でもだらっとしてるみたいですね。なんか、目的とかなく流されてる感じがします。受験を言い出した頃は、イキイキしてたんですけど。
dialogue.English: It seems he's slacking off at school too. I feel like he's just drifting along without any purpose. When he first mentioned taking the exams, he seemed so full of life.

dialogue.content: 元々はそこそこできると思ったんですけど、この生活と態度は、いかがなものかと。
dialogue.English: I thought he was reasonably capable originally, but this lifestyle and attitude... I don't know what to think.

dialogue.content: どんどん合格が遠退く感じです。
dialogue.English: It feels like his chances of passing are getting slimmer and slimmer.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。生活態度があまりよくないのは心配ですね。。。。受験をしたいという気持ちになったきっかけなどあるのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: I see. It's worrying that his attitude toward his daily life isn't very good. Was there something that made him want to take the entrance exams in the first place?

dialogue.content: 3年生まで私立だったのですが、周りの子が普通に受験をする流れでした。
dialogue.English: He was in a private school until the 3rd grade, and it was just the normal thing for the kids around him to take entrance exams.

dialogue.content: 周りのお子さんと息子さんは希望するところが違うんですね
dialogue.English: So, the schools your son is hoping to get into are different from those of the children around him now.

dialogue.content: 今は公立に転校して、授業中に出歩いたり、先生も怒鳴ったり、前はあり得ないって言ってました。今の学校では、受験をするお子さんは、知りませんね。、
dialogue.English: He transferred to a public school, and he said students walk around during class and teachers even yell—things that would have been unthinkable before. At his current school, I don't know of any children who are taking entrance exams.

dialogue.content: そういうことだったんですね。今は転校されて、前の時とは違う状況だったのですね。今は受験する友達がいるかもわからないということなんですね。
dialogue.English: I see, so that's what happened. He's transferred and now the situation is different from before. So you're saying he might not have any friends now who are also taking exams.

dialogue.content: 転校されてから息子さんの様子はどうなんでしょう？
dialogue.English: How has your son been since he transferred?

dialogue.content: だらっとしてます。
dialogue.English: He's been listless.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。前の学校のときはそんなことなかったかんじですか？
dialogue.English: I see. Was he not like that at his previous school?

dialogue.content: 年齢的なこともあるのかと思ってるんですけど、なかったですね。年々憎たらしくなってきます。
dialogue.English: I wonder if it's partly his age, but no, he wasn't like that before. He gets more aggravating every year.

dialogue.content: 態度が。
dialogue.English: His attitude.

dialogue.content: だんだんと知恵がついてきたりして、小さいときのようにはいかなくなり寂しいですよね
dialogue.English: As they get older and a bit wiser, they don't behave like they did when they were little. It can feel a bit sad, can't it?

dialogue.content: 今の学校のお友達の関係などはどんなかんじですか？
dialogue.English: What are his friendships like at his current school?

dialogue.content: また、小学生も5年生ともなれば。そこそこ仲の良い子はいますけど、こちらは塾が多いのであんまり遊びませんね。ゲームの話で気が合うみたいです。
dialogue.English: Well, he is in the 5th grade now. He has some friends he gets along with, but since he has a lot of cram school, he doesn't play with them much. They seem to bond over talking about video games.

dialogue.content: 勉強しないくせに、公立には進みたくないってのは譲らないので困ります。
dialogue.English: Even though he doesn't study, he's adamant that he doesn't want to go to a public middle school, which is a problem.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。公立の学校に嫌気をさしているのですね。転校されたきっかけなどあるのですか？差し支えなければおしえていただけますか？
dialogue.English: I see. So he's taken a dislike to public schools. Was there a particular reason for the transfer? Could you tell me, if you don't mind?

dialogue.content: 夫の転勤で通えなくなりました。単身赴任は考えませんでした。
dialogue.English: We couldn't commute anymore due to my husband's job transfer. We didn't consider him moving alone.

dialogue.content: そうだったのですね。お仕事の都合だと転校もやむを得ないですよね。息子さんが私立の学校に行きたい理由というのはどうしてか聞いたことありますか？
dialogue.English: I see. A transfer is unavoidable when it's for work, isn't it? Have you ever asked your son why he wants to go to a private school?

dialogue.content: そう言えばちゃんとは聞いたことはないですね。3年生の時に受験と言い始めた頃は公立の学校は知りませんでした。転校してすぐの頃は、ギャップを感じていたようです。
dialogue.English: Come to think of it, I haven't really asked properly. When he started talking about entrance exams in third grade, he didn't know about public schools. Right after we transferred, he seemed to feel the gap.

dialogue.content: 私立と公立でだいぶ環境に差があったのでしょうね。お話少し整理させていただきますね
dialogue.English: There must have been quite a difference in the environment between the private and public schools. Let me try to summarize what you've told me so far.

dialogue.content: はあ
dialogue.English: Uh-huh.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 貴子さんは小５の息子さんのことでとても困っていらっしゃいます。
dialogue.English: Takako, you're having a very difficult time with your 5th-grade son.

dialogue.content: 息子さんは受験をしたいということですが、学校での生活態度があまりよくないことや、宿題などしないこと、塾をさぼったりすることがあり、とても心配でいらっしゃいます
dialogue.English: Your son says he wants to take the entrance exams, but you're very worried because his attitude at school isn't good, he doesn't do his homework, and he's started skipping cram school.

dialogue.content: 貴子さんが注意をしても言うことをきかず、いらっとしてしまう日々をお過ごしです。
dialogue.English: Even when you try to correct him, he doesn't listen, and you're spending your days feeling irritated.

dialogue.content: そうです。
dialogue.English: That's right.

dialogue.content: 夫さんの仕事の都合で転校することになり、私立の学校から公立の学校へ変わり、環境もとても変化しています。息子さんは断固として、私立の学校を受験するといっています。
dialogue.English: Due to your husband's work, he had to transfer from a private to a public school, and the environment has changed a lot. Your son is adamant that he will take the private school entrance exam.

dialogue.content: しかし、受験したいというのにもかかわらず勉強もおろそかなことから、応援したいけれど、行動に移さずに困っていらっしゃいます。
dialogue.English: However, despite saying he wants to take the exam, he's neglecting his studies, so although you want to support him, you're troubled that he isn't taking action.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: このようなかんじでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Is that a fair summary?

dialogue.content: 息子さんのこととても心配ですよね。学校のことや進路のこととても大切なことなので、一緒に考えていきましょう
dialogue.English: You must be very worried about your son. His schooling and future path are very important, so let's think about this together.

dialogue.content: そうですね。なんか、私一人でバカらしくなってきました。夫は、また転勤とかなったら…というのが内心あるのかもしれません。
dialogue.English: Yes. I'm starting to feel foolish for worrying about this all by myself. My husband may have the thought "What if there's another transfer?" in the back of his mind.

dialogue.content: はい。今後、どうしていったら良いのでしょうか。
dialogue.English: Yes. What should I do from now on?

dialogue.content: 転勤することがあると、安定しないですもんね。なかなか先を見越せないのもおつらいですよね
dialogue.English: Having to transfer can be very unsettling. It must be difficult not being able to plan for the future.

dialogue.content: 青天の霹靂でした、転勤は。、
dialogue.English: The job transfer was a complete bolt from the blue.

dialogue.content: そうですよね。転勤することによって、家族みんながいろいろと考えなければならなくなりますよね。さきほど貴子さんは息子さんが勉強頑張るなら受験させたいとお考えでしたね。貴子さんは、息子さんのことで一番お困りのことはなんでしょうか？
dialogue.English: I can imagine. A job transfer forces the whole family to rethink many things. You mentioned earlier that if your son studies hard, you want to let him take the exams. What is the biggest difficulty you're facing with your son right now?

dialogue.content: 受験をしたいならしたいで、本気で勉強をしてくれないことです。
dialogue.English: It's that if he says he wants to take the exam, he needs to study for it seriously, but he won't.

dialogue.content: 息子さんには頑張ってほしいですよね。今はとにかく勉強して受験に備えてほしいとお考えなんですね
dialogue.English: You want your son to try his best. So right now, you just want him to study and prepare for the exams.

dialogue.content: はい、後悔はしてほしくないです。
dialogue.English: Yes, I don't want him to have regrets.

dialogue.content: そうですよね。一度しかない人生ですからね。
dialogue.English: That's right. You only get one life, after all.

dialogue.content: 公立でもいいと思ってるなら分かるんですけど、私立に行きたいって言っててこれでは…。
dialogue.English: I would understand if he thought public school was fine, but he says he wants to go to a private school and then acts like this...

dialogue.content: 心配になりますよね。希望があるのに何もしないとなると、どうするの？って感じですよね
dialogue.English: It's worrying, isn't it? When someone has a goal but does nothing to achieve it, it makes you want to ask, "So what are you going to do?"

dialogue.content: なにもしないどころか、それ以下な感じです。
dialogue.English: It feels like it's worse than just doing nothing.

dialogue.content: 貴子さんはとても息子さんの将来のこと考えていらっしゃいます。息子さんのお気持ちを尊重し、受験のことを真剣に悩んでいらっしゃいます。
dialogue.English: Takako, you are thinking so much about your son's future. You're respecting his feelings and are genuinely concerned about his exams.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 息子さんが勉強しないことや注意をしても行動に移さないことでイライラとしてしまうこともあります。それでも、息子さんのことを考えて、いい方向にむくように声をかけていることがわかります
dialogue.English: There are times when you feel irritated that he doesn't study or take action even when you tell him to. Even so, I can see that you're talking to him with his best interests in mind, hoping things will head in a good direction.

dialogue.content: 暖簾に腕押しですけど。
dialogue.English: It's like talking to a brick wall, though.

dialogue.content: 息子さんは、私立から公立へ転校して学校の施設や先生の質など環境に変化を感じていらっしゃると思います
dialogue.English: I think your son is feeling the change in his environment since transferring from a private to a public school—things like the school facilities and the quality of the teachers.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: そして、小５という年代でもあり早い子では反抗期ということも考えられます
dialogue.English: Also, he's in the 5th grade, and for some children, that's when a rebellious phase can begin.

dialogue.content: そうですよね。
dialogue.English: That's true.

dialogue.content: 私の思ったことをお伝えすると
dialogue.English: If I may share my thoughts,

dialogue.content: 受験まではまだ１年あるので、少し様子をみてみるのはいかがでしょうか？
dialogue.English: There's still a year until the exams, so how about waiting and seeing how things go for a little while?

dialogue.content: 手遅れになりませんかね。
dialogue.English: Won't that be too late?

dialogue.content: どれくらい様子を見たらいいんでしょう。
dialogue.English: How long should I wait and see?

dialogue.content: 手遅れになったらという心配もありますよね。受験は高校もありますから・・・・もしかしたら、私立の学校とのギャップについていけないだけなのかと思います。
dialogue.English: I understand your concern about it being too late. There are always high school entrance exams, too... It could be that he's just having trouble coping with the gap between his old private school and his new one.

dialogue.content: 今の学校が、前とはギャップありすぎなんですね。
dialogue.English: The gap between his current school and his old one is just too big, isn't it?

dialogue.content: さきほど先生が怒ったりなどあると言っていたので、そのように感じました。
dialogue.English: You mentioned earlier that teachers yell and so on, which gave me that impression.

dialogue.content: 中学３年間、公立でやっていけるのか小学校以上に心配です。
dialogue.English: I'm even more worried about whether he can handle three years in a public middle school than I am about elementary school.

dialogue.content: 貴子さんが心配という部分もお感じだったのですね。息子さんがどうして私立の学校に行きたいか理由を聞いていなかったとおっしゃていたので、そのことを息子さんに聞いてみて判断してもいいかもしれませんね
dialogue.English: So you were feeling worried about that aspect as well. You mentioned you hadn't asked your son why he wants to go to a private school, so perhaps you could ask him about that and then decide what to do.

dialogue.content: そうですね。改めて動機をハッキリさせたいと思います。
dialogue.English: That's true. I think I'll try to get a clear understanding of his motivation.

dialogue.content: もしかしたら、息子さんのなかにしっかりとした理由があって決めているのかもしれませんね。お話をされてみて、今後のことじっくり話合われるのもいいかもしれないですね。
dialogue.English: Perhaps he has a solid reason and has already made up his mind. It might be a good idea to talk with him and have a thorough discussion about the future.

dialogue.content: 本日お話されてみていかがでしたか？
dialogue.English: How do you feel after talking today?

dialogue.content: はい、分かりました。ついついイライラばかり募ってしまって肝心なことが抜けてました。有り難うございました。
dialogue.English: Yes, I understand now. I was so caught up in my frustration that I was missing the most important thing. Thank you very much.

dialogue.content: 貴子さんがとても息子さんのことを思っていらっしゃると思いますので、焦らずお話できるといいですね。息子さんの進路がいい方向へいくことを願っています
dialogue.English: I can tell you care for your son very much, so I hope you can talk with him without rushing. I hope his future path goes in a good direction.

dialogue.content: そうですね。一度、ゆっくり聞いてみようと思います。
dialogue.English: You're right. I'll try to sit down and listen to him carefully.

dialogue.content: 本日はお話聴かせていただきありがとうございました。これで、ご相談終了させていただきますね。
dialogue.English: Thank you for sharing your story with me today. This will conclude our consultation.

dialogue.content: 今日は有り難うございました。
dialogue.English: Thank you for your time today.

dialogue.content: 本日はご相談いただきありがとうございました
dialogue.English: Thank you for your consultation today.

dialogue.content: （これでロールプレイ終了します。本日はありがとうございました）
dialogue.English: (This concludes the role-play. Thank you for your time today.)

dialogue.content: ■有り難うございました。
dialogue.English: Thank you very much.

dialogue.content: （それでは失礼いたします）
dialogue.English: (I'll take my leave then.)

dialogue.content: ■はい
dialogue.English: Okay.
